analyzed_vuln.description: setcos_create_key frees an sc_file object returned by setcos_new_file/sc_profile_get_file even though that object can contain ACL pointers encoded as non-heap sentinel values (or otherwise non-owned state) from profile/template data. During sc_file_free(), sc_file_clear_acl_entries() iterates file->acl[] and calls free() on an invalid pointer (crash seen at 0x1000002), causing a bad-free. Root cause is ownership/lifetime mismatch in setcos_create_key: it treats template-derived file as fully heap-owned and always safe to deep-free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In fuzz_pkcs15init, attacker-controlled profile/filesystem input is parsed and used by sc_profile_get_file via setcos_new_file when generating an RSA key (do_generate_key -> sc_pkcs15init_generate_key -> profile->ops->create_key -> setcos_create_key). A crafted template/private-key file description can populate ACL fields with malformed/sentinel-like pointer values not allocated by malloc. When setcos_create_key hits an error path (e.g., sc_select_file returns unexpected error) or normal cleanup path and calls sc_file_free(file), sc_file_clear_acl_entries attempts free() on those invalid ACL pointers, triggering ASan bad-free.
